My initial hypothesis is that this could be Powdery Mildew, given the white, spotty appearance. However, I will now examine the reference images to confirm. I will start by looking at one image from each of the four possible classes. My first reference image view will be of Anthracnose.

This presentation is inconsistent with the test image, which features distinct, scattered white spots without large-scale tissue necrosis or holes.

Reference image 2 (Die_Back) analysis: This image shows a completely desiccated, shriveled, and dark necrotic leaf. This represents a much more advanced stage of disease or a completely different pathology compared to the test image, which shows a still-green leaf with surface spots. Die_Back appears to be a poor match.

Now I will examine the reference image for Powdery_Mildew, which I suspect is the correct class.

Reference image 3 (Powdery_Mildew) analysis: This image shows a leaf with a widespread, white-to-greyish powdery coating, formed by many small spots that have started to merge. This pattern and color of symptoms strongly resemble those in the test image, although the infection in the reference image is more severe. This is currently the best match.

I have one reference image view remaining. I will now examine the image for Sooty_Mould to complete my initial survey of all classes.

Reference image 4 (Sooty_Mould) analysis: This image displays dark, black, soot-like patches covering the leaf surface. The color and texture of these symptoms are distinctly different from the white, powdery spots seen on the test image. Sooty_Mould is a poor match.

After reviewing one reference image from each of the four possible classes, the `Powdery_Mildew` reference image is the only one that closely matches the symptoms of small, scattered, white spots seen in the test image. The other classes show vastly different symptoms (large necrotic holes for Anthracnose, desiccation for Die_Back, and black patches for Sooty_Mould). The evidence strongly supports a classification of Powdery Mildew.
